JPMorgan Chase's 2023 Form 10-K (in my library as *JPM_2023_10K.pdf*) discloses the following amounts relating to the January 1, 2023 adoption of the FASB guidance *Financial Instruments – Credit Losses: Troubled Debt Restructurings*, applied under the **modified retrospective method** (i.e., the effect was booked as an adjustment to equity at the effective date, not through earnings):

**1. Effect on the allowance — $587 million decrease (Firm-wide, pre-tax)**
- Note 1, "Accounting standards adopted January 1, 2023" (10-K p.173) and Note 13 (p.256): adoption "resulted in a net decrease to the allowance for credit losses of $587 million," predominantly driven by residential real estate and credit card.
- **What it measures:** the one-time release, at January 1, 2023, of allowances previously carried on troubled loans under the old asset-specific/discounted-cash-flow (DCF) method, as the Firm moved those loans to its non-DCF, portfolio-based allowance approach (the Firm kept the DCF/asset-specific method only for collateral-dependent and nonaccrual risk-rated wholesale loans). Note 13's table (p.258) and the identical MD&A table (p.132) label this the "Cumulative effect of a change in accounting principle" and footnote it as "the impact to the allowance for loan losses upon the adoption." No adjustment was made to the allowance for lending-related commitments.

**2. Same $587 million disaggregated by loan portfolio segment (Note 13, p.258; MD&A p.132)** — these measure the same cumulative-effect adjustment by portfolio:
- Consumer, excluding credit card: **$(489) million**
- Credit card: **$(100) million**
- Wholesale: **$+2 million**
- Total: **$(587) million**

(No separate dollar amount is given for a business segment such as CCB or CB — only the qualitative statement that the change was "predominantly driven by residential real estate and credit card.")

**3. Effect on retained earnings — $446 million increase, after-tax**
- Note 1 (p.173) and Note 13 (p.256): the same adoption "resulted in ... an increase to retained earnings of $446 million, after-tax."
- **What it measures:** the after-tax (net-of-tax) cumulative-effect adjustment to equity recorded directly in retained earnings on the adoption date, reflecting the pre-tax $587 million allowance release net of the related deferred taxes.

**Related figure worth noting:** the Consolidated statements of changes in stockholders' equity (p.169) show a **$449 million** "Cumulative effect of change in accounting principles" line in retained earnings for 2023. That line covers *both* standards adopted January 1, 2023 — the TDR guidance ($446 million after-tax) plus the immaterial retained-earnings effect of the HTM-to-AFS transfer under the Fair Value Hedging – Portfolio Layer Method guidance.

- **Carrying/valuation effects:** The Firm retained ~18.6 million Visa B-2 shares, held at "nominal carryover basis" under the measurement alternative (convertible into Class A at 1.5430 at year-end 2024, subject to significant litigation-related uncertainty); and it holds derivatives associated with 11.6 million Visa B-2 shares from pre-2024 B-share sales, recorded in trading liabilities with fair-value changes in other income.
